note: Claude is called only from the Node server, so no ai_browser_call. No secret_exposure: both env examples hold placeholders, no .env is committed, and the test setup uses a mock Duffel token. cancelFlightOrder and payForHeldOrder in flights.ts are not exposed to the model or MCP. The Amadeus client and request router are dead code. Under the second migration's RLS, the server-side profile tools use the anon key with no user session, so they likely fail on every call. docs/, CLAUDE.md, README, lockfiles and test suites were skipped except for key greps.

labels.what: book_flight creates real Duffel orders straight from model arguments. No spend cap, no per-session booking limit, no duplicate guard. The instant branch pays from the agency balance with a model-supplied amount and currency (141-149) that is never compared to the offer price

book_hotel creates a real Duffel stay booking with no price check and no limit. The 'mock payment method' object is built but never passed (stays-client.ts 81-95), so no payment is collected from the guest
generate_payment_link takes orderId, amount and currency from the model and never checks them against the Duffel order. The amount drives the payment modal and the URL
update_user_profile upserts name, email, phone, birth date and gender for any model-chosen device_id. No identity binding and no format checks

book_flight holds or buys a ticket with no confirmation step. A click on a flight card sends 'I would like to book' (ChatInterface.js 72-77), and the prompt says to book immediately from saved profile data and to guess title and gender from the first name
book_hotel books a room straight from the model call, with no customer confirmation or payment step
Prompt orders the model to chain book_flight into generate_payment_link and to 'NEVER ask user permission'
Personal details are saved 'as a background operation' with no user approval (prompt lines 95, 119-126)
get_payment_status never calls Duffel. It always returns status 'pending' (comment: 'For now, we'll return a mock status')
When the offer needs instant payment, book_flight returns success true with booking_reference 'PENDING_PAYMENT' and the offer id as order_id, though nothing was booked

'DO NOT call book_flight multiple times' is only a prompt line. The ReAct loop runs up to 5 rounds and executes every book_flight call with no duplicate check. The follow-up Claude calls (239-244, 314-320) send no system prompt, so after round one the rule survives only as a user-role reminder (225)
Prompt says to pass the amount and currency from the booking response. generate_payment_link accepts any amount the model sends
Prompt says dates must be in the future. searchFlights passes dates through with no check
The device_id scheme ('web_session_' + timestamp) exists only in the prompt. The profile tools accept any device_id, so one user can read or overwrite another's profile
POST /api/payment-intents/:id/confirm always returns status 'succeeded' from a mock function. No payment is confirmed
createPaymentIntent invents ids like pi_<timestamp> and status 'requires_card_details'. No payment intent exists at Duffel
The 'Profile information saved' status is sent before the result is checked, so it shows even when the save fails. Under the RLS policies the anon server client cannot write device_id rows
Standalone payment page for offers that need instant payment shows 'Secure Payment Ready' and 'For demo purposes' text with no card form. Nothing can be paid
Shows 'Payment Successful! Your booking is confirmed. You will receive details via email' after card entry, but the server never charges the card. The agency balance pays and the app sends no email
POST /api/process-payment has no login check. Anyone who sends an offer or order id gets it booked and paid from the agency Duffel balance, with passenger details taken from the request body
POST /clear_chat has no auth and wipes every connected user's chat history
/api/component-client-key and /api/payment-intents have no auth. Anyone can mint Duffel component keys and look up any order's amount by id
WebSocket has no authentication. The server trusts the client-sent isAuthenticated flag and profile object (sent from ChatInterface.js 74-77) and tells the model the user is authenticated
get_user_profile returns any stored profile (name, email, phone, birth date) for whatever device_id the model passes, with no binding to the caller
user_profiles (PII) created with no row level security. RLS and own-row policies arrive only in the next migration
Supabase anon key read from REACT_APP_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY in browser code. Public by design. The .env.example holds a placeholder only
cors() with no options allows every origin on all routes, including the payment endpoints

card_id from the card form is accepted but never used. Every payment is made with payment_type 'balance' (agency funds), and the 3DS helper in flight-client.ts 187 is never called, so the customer is never charged

Client-sent profile fields are joined into a '[SYSTEM CONTEXT]' message that the prompt tells the model to trust and book from. A user can also type '[SYSTEM CONTEXT]' text. Both are prompt injection paths into booking
No rate limit or connection limit on the chat socket. Each message can run up to 5 tool rounds with 2 Claude calls each
Amount and currency shown on the payment page come from URL parameters. The client never sends expected_amount, so the server's price check (http-server.ts 108-115) never runs
Full booking arguments are logged, including passenger name, email, phone and birth date. Also flight-client.ts 115 and 232, and the tool arg and result logs in websocket-server.ts 188, 238 and 456
The full chat, including passenger details, is saved to localStorage
Card form results are written to the browser console (also line 123)
Fallback builds the payment modal order id and amount by regex over the model's free text, so the price shown comes from model output
Search always asks for one adult. The adults argument is ignored, so prices and holds cover one passenger whatever the user asked
Model id 'claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022' and max_tokens 3000 hardcoded, repeated at 240-241 and 315-316
FRONTEND_URL falls back to http://localhost:8080. Same fallback in flights.ts 305
Hotel payment currency hardcoded to USD. Guest age is hardcoded to 25 in stays-client.ts 30
Payment intent currency defaults to USD and payment_type is hardcoded to 'balance' at 142 and 150
ReAct loop cap of 5 rounds and the 20-message history window (claude-client.ts 144) are hardcoded
Amadeus credentials are required at startup, but the Amadeus client and the request router are never imported by the running app
Hardcoded airport, airline, cabin and hotel amenity lists. They are not wired to any MCP handler
